accepted_contract: Exactly one optional PageDefinition.loadHtml(url, signal):Promise<string> field is added. The function is read and validated once per mount, invoked plainly, and reused for reload. No other declaration snapshot guarantee is introduced.

Native Fetch remains the omitted-loader path. URL HTML from both paths uses the same one-element parser, recursive executable checks including nested HTML template contents, live ID checks, generation checks, controller lifetime, and cleanup. Inert template IDs keep their existing semantics.

Borrowed and factory roots do not invoke loadHtml. Custom FrameworkError and AbortError values retain their origin. Nonfunction options and nontext results have explicit Page errors; ordinary default body-read errors retain PAGE_INIT.

The same complete definition composes with main content, Popup, Tabs, and Documents through the existing runner. Real HTTP/communicator witnesses assert prepared headers and transformed text across all four containers.

Caller-owned staging hosts implement destination/add or retain-old replacement. Candidate ready already includes activation, old retirement is a commit boundary, and the application disposes failed/superseded handles and removes their hosts. No generic replacement or loader registry is added.

Installed browser JavaScript executes captured loader, communicator, reload, abort, inert-ID, nested-executable, and disposal outcomes; the installed TypeScript fixture accepts text loaders and rejects Response-returning loaders. Existing M3.2 request witnesses remain present.
review_findings_resolved: The first plain-receiver fixture ran a sloppy callback through page.evaluate. An explicit strict directive now tests undefined receiver on an actual plain call. Page API now distinguishes runner-created errors from propagated FrameworkError values, states default body-read PAGE_INIT, and limits capture/mutation guarantees to loadHtml.
The container recipe explicitly assigns child-host removal to the application.
